title: Assail
author: Ian C. Esslemont
review:
3.5/5 Solid and enjoyable, had a bit higher expectations for some of the lore implications so it might have let me down a bit there but overall a really fun time on a continent we've never seen before.

His last two books I connected with a bit more but this one had some good stuff, just sort of continues the issues where it'd be a bit stronger if he cut a couple POVs and focused on some a bit more.

I'm definitely going to continue with Path to Ascendency and also retry Kharkhanas again in the future, love the Malazan setting and world and it's fun to be more caught up with all the lore.

highlights.text: ‘My friend, if in some manner you find yourself disadvantaged by the law then by definition you must be a criminal.’
Yet this was also Assail, and many stories told of what else lurked in these mist-shrouded mountain forests. Stories that he knew contained a terrifying truth at their root: raw power itself.
‘Say what you will of me,’ he shouted, ‘but do not insult my father’s name! You who cowered in the warmth of your hearthfire while he kept watch!’ ‘Conspired with the mountain demons, you mean,’
‘Take my advice, lad,’ he said. ‘Don’t get caught up in all this talk of missions and god-given purposes. I’ve seen it before and it only leads to misery and pain.’

The storied creators of winter itself in the times of heroes. He found these curtains and graceful banners breathtakingly beautiful. He’d always admired the lights. Especially those few winters when he’d trapped and hunted the borders of the Holdings with his father. It was consoling to see them now, somehow. As if he’d come home. Home to where he belonged.
Arrow after arrow punched into Coots. ‘Hey … now…’ he said, sounding very disappointed. He tumbled backwards.
‘I just realized that I’ve risked everything to reach a destination I don’t even want to be at.’
‘That’s what journeys are for, my love. You have to take the path to learn where you want to be.’

An open-air graveyard where the dead were obviously simply thrown from the docks and shore. Hordes of ghost-crabs wandered from corpse to corpse like clouds of locusts, gorging themselves. The ragged fortune-hunters who crowded the dock waving and shouting were no more reassuring. Ragged and starving they were, in tattered shirts and canvas trousers, with mud-caked bare feet. They shouted their services as stevedores. Jute wouldn’t trust a pot of shit to any one of them.
‘I saved your life, you old fool.’ Old Bear waved a dismissal over the fallen men. ‘All you did was cheat me of a great boast – should I have succeeded.’

Even regions that boast of themselves as ‘pure’ or ‘native’ stand upon the bones of forgotten predecessors. But he was a bard – he could not forget, nor would he. Now the same inexorable story had finally reached his homeland.
We have faith in Togg, my friend, absent though he may be. All shall be as he foretold. Never fear. Our fate has not come yet … but it shall.’
‘Why, everyone knows about their ways. “Forkrulan justice” is a saying for any harsh, but just, judgement.’

All I have are suspicions, hints, lines from old sagas, but what I dread may be very real. I fear both what lies ahead and what lies behind. And for the life of me, I cannot say which is the lesser of the two! Omtose Phellack is stirring. And why? What could raise its ire?

The ignorant speak of the winters of the Stormriders and the Jaghut as if they are the same thing. But that is not so. The Riders are alien. Not of this world. Indeed, some argue that in their original form they were of the frigid black gaps between the worlds – but that cannot be decided.
